description: Replace terminal AgentSession events with a reusable Turn lifecycle across the Server, Runner, and Web.

tasks.title: Implement Server Turn protocol and Session migration
tasks.description: Make the Session bounded context the authoritative interpreter for Turn and Follow-up facts. Replace terminal Session state and close-specific grain operations with Turn activity, binding, current/latest Turn summaries, operation fences, Turn-keyed transcript persistence, and Session command/API contracts. Add the schema/startup migration, legacy Follow-up migration resolver, and version-2 Runner admission gate that convert persisted state and reject mismatched runners before new protocol traffic is admitted.
acceptanceCriteria: The Session grain accepts only canonical `turn.*` and `followup.*` execution facts, enforces stable Turn identity, per-Turn ordering, one start, at most one finish, and rejects legacy terminal event names.

Finished Turns leave the logical Session idle with its Runtime binding intact; missing bindings, unknown activity, Follow-up, Cancel, Compact, and Reset use the specified eligibility rules without changing TaskRun or AgentJob work results.

Follow-up reservations persist stable operation and new-Turn identities, atomically record admitted input facts, retain ambiguous delivery for reconciliation, and never automatically resend uncertain Runtime input.

The EF schema and startup migration group legacy Follow-up transcript facts by operation, atomically write admitted plus started for each persisted input, and project unprovable in-flight execution as `unknown` without an admitted fact.

A version-2-only Server migration resolver remains admissible across restart and after initial cutover, consumes one Runner migration-resolution record per legacy Follow-up group, acknowledges an already migrated admitted pair idempotently, and otherwise records delivery-unconfirmed without accepting any legacy runtime event name.

Runner registration, heartbeat, runtime-event upload, poll, and Hub tracking require `sessionProtocolVersion: 2`; missing or mismatched versions return `runner_session_protocol_incompatible`, leave the runner unavailable, and cannot receive Session commands.

Server unit and spec coverage exercises Turn invariants, command gates, Follow-up state convergence, legacy-event rejection, migrated transcript state, matching/mismatched Runner protocol admission, and a late upgraded Runner resolving a record after Server restart; `npm test` passes.
tasks.output: Server Session domain, transcript persistence, API contracts, and durable migration implementing the Turn protocol.
tasks.notes: Persist the runner protocol version in RunnerInfo and enforce it on both REST and Hub entry points; do not retain legacy event compatibility after migration.

tasks.title: Migrate Runner Turn reporting and durable delivery
tasks.description: Update OpenCode and Pi execution reporters, AgentJob execution, workflow actions, Follow-up handling, Cancel outcomes, and the shared runtime-event outbox to produce the Server Turn protocol. Version and migrate Runner outbox snapshots before delivery by grouping legacy records per Follow-up operation and replacing each group with a durable migration-resolution record; the Server, not the Runner, classifies persisted-input groups as admitted-plus-started and all other groups as delivery-unconfirmed without rerunning Runtime input.
acceptanceCriteria: OpenCode and Pi emit replay-stable Turn IDs and the same `turn.started`, Turn-scoped runtime facts, and `turn.finished` outcomes for Workflow and AgentJob execution.

Runner Follow-up handling emits admitted, rejected, or delivery-unconfirmed facts with the original operation and Turn identities; it never emits legacy Follow-up terminal events or re-invokes an ambiguous Runtime operation.
Cancel and failure paths report confirmed Turn outcomes only; inability to confirm Runtime stop leaves the Server able to project `unknown` rather than receiving a fabricated terminal event.

The outbox replaces each v1 Follow-up group with one ordered, durable migration-resolution record before it becomes ready; it preserves group identity and acknowledgement semantics, never emits admitted itself, and invokes no duplicate Runtime input.

The indefinitely admissible version-2-only Server migration resolver classifies each migration-resolution record against migrated transcript evidence, returns the existing admitted-plus-started pair only for a persisted input, and otherwise atomically records delivery-unconfirmed for absent-input, unusable-identity, and failed-only groups.

The host supplies `sessionProtocolVersion: 2` on registration, heartbeat, and Hub setup, and treats protocol incompatibility as a permanent unavailable state that prevents outbox drain, polling, and Session-command handling.

Runner unit/spec coverage covers both runtimes, workflow and AgentJob paths, active/idle Follow-up, ambiguity, cancellation, every legacy Follow-up group classification, v1 outbox crash recovery, matching/mismatched protocol admission, late upgrade after Server restart, and legacy-event removal; `npm run typecheck -w packages/runner` and `npm test -w packages/runner` pass.
tasks.output: Runner protocol producers and versioned outbox migration compatible with the Server Turn contract.
tasks.notes: Use the protocol-version gate supplied by T-001; do not implement a legacy fallback, dual-write path, or automatic retry of a migration-unconfirmed operation.

tasks.title: Project reusable Sessions in API and Web
tasks.description: Expose the Server's activity, binding, current Turn, latest Turn, and command eligibility projections through canonical Session DTOs and update AgentOps/read routes accordingly. Replace Web legacy event handling, transcript reconstruction, session lists, details, status displays, and controls so users see a reusable Session and its latest Turn rather than a terminal Session result.
acceptanceCriteria: Session API and AgentOps/read projections expose independent activity, binding, current Turn, latest Turn, and command eligibility; they do not expose normal Session completion, failure, or closure derived from historical Turn results.
Web canonical event types and live handlers consume the Turn and Follow-up protocol exclusively and remove handling for `session.closed`, `session.followup_completed`, and `session.followup_failed`.

Transcript, session list, detail, and composer views show recent Turn outcomes while allowing an idle bound Session to start another Turn; unknown and missing-binding states block or present the correct recovery controls.
Server route/DTO coverage and Web unit/spec coverage cover completed, failed, stopped, unknown, missing-binding, active Follow-up, idle Follow-up, and live event updates.
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` pass.
tasks.output: Updated Session read APIs, AgentOps projections, and Web Session experience for reusable Turn-based conversations.
tasks.notes: T-003 can proceed in parallel with T-002 after the Server contract is available; it consumes canonical Server projections rather than deriving state from raw terminal events.
